bytes.kicker: What managements talk about · Q4 FY26 → Q2 FY27 calls
bytes.title: Tariff talk is fading. Defence and data centres are rising.
bytes.dek: With US tariffs on India cut to 18% under the February 2026 trade deal and talks still running, tariffs came up on 22.5% of Q2 calls, down from 32.3% two quarters ago.
bytes.read: Managements have stopped explaining tariffs and started talking about where new orders come from: defence, data centres and customers moving supply chains to India.
bytes.sources: Vantage theme tracker across ~1,100 calls a quarter (BSE filings), as of 18 Nov 2026; tariff level: White House fact sheet on the US–India trade deal, Feb 2026
bytes.notes: Each call is tagged with the themes management discusses; a theme's share is the % of that quarter's calls that mention it. Shown: the six biggest risers and six biggest fallers between Q4 FY26 (calls in Apr–Jun 2026) and Q2 FY27 (Oct–Nov 2026). A mention is not a forecast: tariffs falling off calls means less discussion, not that tariff risk is gone. Open Themes on the dashboard for the companies behind each theme.

stats.label: Calls discussing tariffs
stats.note: 369 calls in Q4 FY26, 306 in Q1 FY27, 254 in Q2 FY27.

stats.label: Defence indigenisation
stats.note: Mentioned on 93 Q2 FY27 calls, up from 80; mostly industrial and defence suppliers.

stats.label: Data-centre power & cooling
stats.note: 110 Q2 FY27 calls, led by electrical equipment and industrial products makers.

bytes.kicker: Q2 FY27 results scorecard · 2,215 companies with margin data
bytes.title: Sales grew in every sector. Margins went nowhere.
bytes.dek: With the results deadline past, the median company grew revenue 16.9% year on year, but its operating margin moved just +0.1 points.
bytes.read: Growth came through at the top line but not into margins: costs and pricing absorbed most of it, so earnings grew roughly in line with sales.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE (consolidated where available), as of 18 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: Revenue growth and operating (EBITDA) margin are year on year, Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26, using each company's filed results. Medians, so a few large companies do not move the number. Banks and financial services are left out because their 'operating margin' is not comparable; sectors shown are the 14 with the most results filed. Open Results on the dashboard for every company.

stats.label: Half widened margins, half didn't
stats.note: 1,118 of 2,215 widened operating margin year on year; the rest held or shrank.

stats.label: Autos & components
stats.note: The fastest sales growth of any sector, yet the median margin slipped. 144 companies reported.

stats.label: Capital goods
stats.note: The largest group (499 companies): strong order-led growth with flat margins.

bytes.title: Only a third of stocks beat the market on results day.
bytes.dek: Even companies that grew profit 75% or more beat the index on the day after results only 46% of the time. The market wanted more than growth.
bytes.read: This season the bar was set before the numbers came out: misses were sold hard, and big beats were mostly already in the price.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and NSE/BSE closing prices, as of 18 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: Day-one reaction = the stock's move from the close before results to the close on the first trading day after, minus the benchmark index's move over the same day. Profit growth is net profit, Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26; companies with no profit comparison are left out of the groups but counted in the overall share. Banks are excluded. Past reactions say nothing about future returns.

stats.label: Beat the index, all results
stats.note: 943 of 2,776 stocks outperformed the index on day one; the median stock lagged by 1.3%.

stats.label: Profit up 75% or more
stats.note: Strong growth barely tilted the odds: median day-one move -0.3% vs the index (387 stocks).

stats.label: Profit down 25% or more
stats.note: Misses were punished: median day-one move -2.5% vs the index (489 stocks).

bytes.kicker: Guidance direction · 1,128 Q2 FY27 calls read
bytes.title: Lenders guide up. Chemicals and FMCG guide down.
bytes.dek: Across 1,128 calls, 44% of managements cut or guided lower and 34% raised or guided higher. The split runs by sector, not by market.
bytes.read: Guidance is splitting by sector: lenders and auto makers sound confident, while chemicals, FMCG and IT are lowering the bar for H2.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of 1,128 Q2 FY27 earnings calls (BSE filings), as of 18 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: How it is counted: a call counts as raising when management raised a number it had guided before, or gave guidance that reads as positive; it counts as cutting when it cut a guided number or gave guidance that reads as negative. A call can count on both sides. Net = % raising − % cutting, per sector, for sectors with at least 25 Q2 FY27 calls read. Open Sectors → Guidance leaders for the companies behind each bar.

stats.label: Cut vs raised, all sectors
stats.note: 492 of 1,128 calls cut or guided lower; 387 raised or guided higher.

stats.label: Financial Services, net
stats.note: 64 of 144 lenders and financiers raised or guided up; 36 cut.

stats.label: Chemicals, net
stats.note: 46 of 73 chemical companies cut or guided lower; only 15 raised.
